overview.short_description: ThingOS is a hybrid-kernel, graph-centric OS where the kernel hosts a semantic graph ('Thing Model') and userland apps interact via syscalls. It features a custom compositor and widget toolkit.

issues.title: Kernel-Graph Coupling
issues.summary: The graph store is embedded in the kernel, violating microkernel principles and creating a large attack surface.
suggested_next_steps: Define a strict interface for the graph store.
Plan migration to a userland service.

issues.title: Unsafe Static Mutables
issues.summary: Usage of `static mut` for global state (caches, backbuffers) creates data race risks.

issues.title: Unsafe Syscall Boundary Hardened (Partial)
issues.summary: Syscall pointer handling now uses validated helpers and minimized unsafe blocks; some high-risk sites remain.
suggested_next_steps: Complete address-range validation for all user pointers.
Add fuzz tests for syscall input combinations.

issues.title: Heap Region Instrumented and Guarded (Partial)
issues.summary: Heap region initialization is now logged; bump allocator has better guard rails; stack guard pages are designed but not fully implemented.
suggested_next_steps: Resolve any documented heap region overlaps.
Implement real guard pages for kernel stacks.

issues.title: Compositor God Object
issues.summary: The `compositor.rs` file is ~3600 lines and handles too many responsibilities (layout, rendering, events).

issues.title: Fixed Stack Sizes
issues.summary: Tasks have fixed 256KB stacks with no overflow protection.

strengths.title: Unified Graph Abstraction
strengths.summary: Consistent use of the graph model for system state and IPC.

strengths.title: Reactive UI Updates
strengths.summary: Use of `WatchManager` to decouple rendering from state changes.

test_recommendations.title: Boot Smoke Test
test_recommendations.summary: Automated QEMU boot that checks for 'Kernel started!' log message.

test_recommendations.title: Syscall Fuzzing
test_recommendations.summary: Basic fuzzing of syscall inputs to ensure kernel stability.
